clue.text: Country soldier, one in Italian city

parts.note: Peru is a South American country
GI is an American soldier
A means one, as in 'a dozen'

explanation.surface: A soldier from the countryside is stationed in a town in Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country soldier' reads like a rustic trooper, but Country is PERU and soldier is GI, with A for 'one'.
explanation.definitionFit: Perugia is the capital of Umbria in central Italy, so it is an Italian city.

clue.text: See 5
Right to come in, keeping one person on a fixed income

indicators.note: keeping means holding something inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: to come in means to enter
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone with a fixed income claims the right to come in and keep a room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeping' puts I inside ENTER, after R for Right.
explanation.definitionFit: A rentier lives on unearned income such as rents or interest from investments, typically a fixed sum.

clue.text: Dress up student intelligence for chance listener: king to phone for painting book

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word for dress is read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: to rig is to dress or kit out
L is the learner plate, used for a student
wit means intelligence or quick thinking
hap is an old word for chance or luck
the ear is the organ of listening
Lear is the king of Shakespeare's tragedy
to ring someone is to phone them

explanation.surface: A jumble of instructions about dressing up, eavesdropping and phoning a king somehow arrives at a painting and a book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns RIG into GIR. The pieces run on in order; 'for' and 'to' are just link words. The king is Shakespeare's Lear, not R.
explanation.definitionFit: Vermeer's famous painting gave its title to Tracy Chevalier's novel, so the phrase names both a painting and a book.

clue.text: Cult of an odd sect cured sorrow — start to cheer!

indicators.note: odd suggests something out of the ordinary, so the word sect is put into another order
cured as in treated or processed, so the letters of sorrow are worked into a new form

parts.note: hip is the opening of the cheer 'hip hip hooray'

explanation.surface: A strange sect cures grief and urges everyone to cheer up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd' rearranges SECT into CEST after AN, 'cured' rearranges SORROW into ORWORS, and 'start to cheer' is HIP, as in 'hip hip hooray', not the letter C.
explanation.definitionFit: Veneration of forebears is a religious practice found in many cultures, so it counts as a cult in the sense of a form of worship.

clue.text: Reported attempt on playwright's taxi

indicators.note: reported means spoken of, so the word for attempt is given by how it is said

parts.note: an attempt is a try
George Bernard Shaw was the Irish playwright

explanation.surface: Someone is said to have tried hailing George Bernard Shaw's cab.
explanation.walkthrough: TRY said out loud gives TRI, the start of the answer; the 's of playwright's is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A trishaw is a three-wheeled pedal cab used to carry passengers in Asian cities, a kind of taxi.

clue.text: Devoted to health, no? Word is, antiphlogistine will be needed

definitions.text: Devoted to health, no? Word is, antiphlogistine will be needed

indicators.note: will be needed hints that the clue's words must be put to fresh use, so all their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Health fanatics are warned that they'll end up needing a soothing poultice.
explanation.walkthrough: Every letter of the clue except 'will be needed' is the anagram fodder, 38 letters. Antiphlogistine is an anti-inflammatory poultice: the burning on that road will need it, which is the &lit joke.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb says good aims alone lead to ruin, and the whole clue jokes that the burning destination will need a soothing remedy.

clue.text: Former minister swallowing ire maybe was too fast

indicators.note: swallowing means taking something inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: Douglas Hurd was a British Home Secretary and Foreign Secretary

indicators.note: maybe signals that the letters of ire are only one possible arrangement, so they are shuffled

explanation.surface: A one-time government minister gulped down his anger and acted rashly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maybe' rearranges IRE into RIE. Douglas Hurd was a Conservative Home and Foreign Secretary in the 1980s and 90s.
explanation.definitionFit: To have hurried is to have moved or acted with excessive speed, which is going too fast.

clue.text: Smart Alick is in the Guardian, getting some rope

indicators.note: in means one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a newspaper refers to itself in editorials as 'we', so the Guardian is WE
a guy is a rope used to steady a tent or mast

explanation.surface: A know-all at the Guardian is given enough rope to hang himself.
explanation.walkthrough: Newspapers speak in leaders with the editorial 'we', so 'the Guardian', the setter's own paper, is WE.
explanation.definitionFit: A wise guy is a slang term for a cocky know-all, just like a smart alec.

clue.text: Chamber separating Turkey and Luxembourg in Italian city

indicators.note: in means the pieces go inside the city's name
separating says the city's letters split the two other pieces apart

parts.note: Venice is the canal city in north-east Italy
TR is the international vehicle code for Turkey
L is the international vehicle code for Luxembourg

explanation.surface: A council chamber sits between Turkish and Luxembourg delegations in Venice.
explanation.walkthrough: The city keeps its own letters IC between the two codes, which is why 'separating' fits: Turkey goes in first, then Luxembourg.
explanation.definitionFit: A ventricle is a hollow cavity of the heart or brain, a chamber in the anatomical sense.

clue.text: Ring in reactor sounds like a bull

indicators.note: sounds like says the answer is said the same as the word for the bull

parts.note: Taurus is the bull of the zodiac

explanation.surface: A ring inside a nuclear reactor is said to resemble a bull.
explanation.walkthrough: TAURUS, the zodiac's bull, said out loud gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A torus is a doughnut-shaped ring, the shape of the vessel in a tokamak fusion reactor.

clue.text: Raised area where flower's not unknown

indicators.note: not says one piece is to be left out of the flower

parts.note: a daisy is a flower; the 's stands for 'is'
Y is an algebraic unknown, like x and z

explanation.surface: Where a raised platform stands, the flower is not unknown.
explanation.walkthrough: In mathematics x, y and z are the unknowns; 'not' removes Y from DAISY.
explanation.definitionFit: A dais is a raised platform at one end of a hall, a raised area for speakers or high table.

clue.text: Very remarkable time in a test of depth

indicators.note: in means one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a sounding is a measurement of the depth of water

explanation.surface: Something amazing happens during a depth measurement.
explanation.walkthrough: A sounding, a measurement of water depth, takes T inside, after A.
explanation.definitionFit: Astounding means so surprising as to stun, a strong synonym of very remarkable.

clue.text: See 3
Our turn round where the rubbish goes in Italian city

indicators.note: round means one piece wraps around the other
turn means twisting the letters of our into a new order

parts.note: a bin is where rubbish is thrown

explanation.surface: We turn round to see where the rubbish ends up in an Italian town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn' rearranges OUR into URO. 'round' looks as if it goes with 'turn' (turn round), but it is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Urbino is a Renaissance hill town in the Marche region of Italy, birthplace of Raphael.

clue.text: Pathetic fellow and prohibitionist: just let them hang

parts.note: a drip is a feeble, wet person
a dry is someone opposed to alcohol, an advocate of prohibition

explanation.surface: A wimp and a teetotaller are left dangling.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is an instruction found on clothing labels: no ironing needed, just hang the garment up.
explanation.definitionFit: Drip-dry clothes need no wringing or ironing; you simply hang them up wet to dry smooth.

clue.text: One church's method of entertainment

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
CE is the Church of England, and the 's adds S
how means the method or manner of doing something

explanation.surface: A single church's way of putting on entertainment.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'church's' contributes its S: I + CE + S + HOW.
explanation.definitionFit: An ice show is a spectacle of skating performers, a form of public entertainment.

clue.text: Sugar maker in use outside American city

indicators.note: outside means the words in use wrap around the other piece

parts.note: LA is Los Angeles

explanation.surface: A sugar refinery is in operation outside an American city.
explanation.walkthrough: IN USE splits around LA: INU-LA-SE.
explanation.definitionFit: Inulase is an enzyme that breaks down inulin to produce fructose, so it makes a sugar.

clue.text: See 3
Far from plain talk about name

indicators.note: about means going round, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: to orate is to talk formally, making a speech

explanation.surface: Speech that dwells on a name is anything but plain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts ORATE round N.
explanation.definitionFit: Ornate means elaborately decorated, the opposite of plain.

clue.text: I'm going to hedge

parts.note: spoken by a garden tool about to clip a hedge, or by a politician who hedges his bets

explanation.surface: Someone announces that they are going to avoid committing themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: Hedge works two ways: cutting a garden hedge, and hedging in argument; a trimmer is also an old term for a politician who changes sides to suit the times.
explanation.definitionFit: A hedge clipper is a garden tool, and a political fence-sitter is someone who hedges to suit the wind.

clue.text: Kept quiet when punter rode off

indicators.note: off means gone wrong or out of order, so the letters of punter rode are rearranged

explanation.surface: A gambler rode off without anyone hearing about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges the ten letters of PUNTER RODE.
explanation.definitionFit: Unreported means not made known publicly, so it was kept quiet.

clue.text: See 5
Old socks picked first off

indicators.note: first off says the opening letter of the word for picked is removed

parts.note: picked means selected, chosen

explanation.surface: Some old socks were selected, and the first one discarded.
explanation.walkthrough: The word for picked loses its first letter C.
explanation.definitionFit: Hosen is the archaic plural of hose, meaning stockings or leg coverings, hence old socks.

clue.text: See 5
The soul of man, I maintain

indicators.note: of says the answer is taken from within the words that follow

explanation.surface: Someone asserts the existence of the human soul.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'mAN I MAintain'.
explanation.definitionFit: In Jungian psychology the anima is the inner self or soul, and in Latin anima means soul.

clue.text: Greeting to Western parents on 1/11

parts.note: hallo is a greeting, a variant of hello
mas are mothers, so parents

explanation.surface: A hello to western parents on the first of November.
explanation.walkthrough: 1/11 is the British date style for 1 November, All Saints' Day.
explanation.definitionFit: Hallowmas is the old name for All Saints' Day, the feast held on 1 November.

clue.text: Spicy drink to urge on the other side

parts.note: to egg someone on is to urge them on
the flip side is the other side of a record or coin

explanation.surface: Encouraging someone to cross to the other side over a hot drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' links the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: An egg flip is a hot drink of beaten egg with spiced ale or wine, an eggnog.

clue.text: 3 nearly meets boy, having points to press?

indicators.note: nearly means the girl's name is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: 3 refers to the first word of the answer to 3 down, a girl; Sadie is a girl's name
Ron is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A young woman almost meets a boy who is armed with points to make.
explanation.walkthrough: The 3 points to the first word of 3 down, a girl, here SADIE; 'nearly' drops its E. The definition is cryptic: a sadiron is pointed at both ends.
explanation.definitionFit: A sadiron is a solid flat iron for pressing clothes, often pointed at both ends.
